1	# ADR 0002: Fixture mode as a synthetic provider
2	
3	**Status:** Proposed
4	
5	## Question and recommendation
6	
7	Investigate replacing the native fixture store/worker with `GmailCore` and a built-in, credential-free `SyntheticProvider`. This is a decision spike, not authorization to change production behavior. Baseline: `58e0bc7`.
8	
9	**Recommendation: GO for staged unification; NO-GO for an unmodified provider-only substitution.** GmailCore already accepts `Arc<dyn GmailReadProvider>` and an injected clock. The provider must own durable synthetic provider facts; the core needs a small explicit fixture policy for mode/capabilities/lifecycle and reminders. Keeping a second operation ledger is avoidable, but silently changing the fixture contract is not acceptable. After those gates, delete the fixture `Store`, worker, reminder implementation and `MailCore` facade, and hold one `GmailCore` in shell state with a session policy instead of the `Backend` enum. Move the 18-conversation data out of `seed.rs` into the synthetic module before deleting that file. Retain shared `CancelToken` infrastructure currently located in `provider.rs`; removing the old archive fake must not remove Gmail cancellation support.
10	
11	## Evidence checkpoints
12	
13	- Required architecture, status, development and ADR 0001 read. Current docs explicitly promise a separate durable native fixture profile, seed-once behavior, archive-only mailbox actions, local drafts and synthetic attachment transfers.
14	- `gmail/sync.rs::open_with_clock` has no direct OAuth/Keychain dependency: those belong to the injected production `GmailProvider`. Startup currently interprets `has_credentials()` as a restore signal; a synthetic implementation needs an explicit local-ready policy rather than inventing real credentials.
15	- `gmail/sync.rs::account_status` hardcodes `MailMode::Gmail`; `mutation_access()` is a Boolean grant covering archive/read/star. Neither preserves fixture wire behavior by itself.
16	- All requested fixture test files were inventoried by test function name (appendix below). No production files are changed by this spike.
17	
18	## Implementation stages (each must remain green and shippable)
19	
20	1. Port fixture-specific guarantees to tests against GmailCore, retain both existing backends, and add a production synthetic data/provider module independent of test support. Keep the default fixture path unchanged.
21	2. Introduce explicit internal session policy in GmailCore: fixture identity/status, archive-only admission, unsupported errors, cached-only search, local readiness and non-destructive lifecycle. Implement persistent synthetic provider facts and seed-once discovery including the two initially archived conversations. Keep Gmail policy unchanged.
22	3. Resolve reminder behavior explicitly and cover it with acceptance/race/restart tests; move synthetic attachments/reply metadata behind provider/core seams. Preserve local drafts and fixture profile safety. Add opt-in synthetic-core launch path for validation.
23	4. Switch fixture default only after all mapped guarantees pass and profile transition disclosure is implemented. Keep the old database as backup. Remove the legacy backend after parity validation; update current docs and browser contract tests. Coordinating thread owns end-to-end validation and merge sequencing.
24	
25	## Risks and decision gates
26	
27	A fresh provider seeded into memory on every launch can overwrite archived provider facts at the next sync. Gmail discovery only lists Inbox, so it cannot by itself reproduce the two archived seed threads. GmailCore may expose read/star or destructive disconnect if fixture mode is represented as Gmail. Reminder scheduling currently has different mailbox effects. These are design gates for implementation, not bugs established by this spike.
28	
29	The prototype will be published separately at [maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/tree/maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype), marked throwaway and not for merge. This PR contains only this ADR.
30	
31	## Behavior inventory and required policy
32	
33	References are repository-relative; function names identify the reviewed seam. **Blocker** means an unmodified provider-only substitution cannot preserve the contract. It does not mean the staged implementation is infeasible.
34	
35	| Surface | Fixture today / GmailCore with synthetic provider | Classification and implementation condition |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| Account/status | `src-tauri/src/main.rs::Backend::account_status` returns fixture/Connected/Idle, no mutation grant, 18 cached, complete, no timestamp, limit 0. `gmail/sync.rs::account_status` returns Gmail, observed grant, transient Authenticating/Syncing, timestamps and limit 100. | **Blocker** to drop-in. Internal fixture policy must retain fixture mode/identity/capability presentation; disclose initial loading if asynchronous bootstrap is retained. Do not masquerade as a connected Google account. |
38	| Credentials | Fixture never opens OAuth or Keychain. GmailCore only calls provider methods; shell constructs GmailProvider/Keychain only in Gmail branch. `gmail/types.rs::GmailReadProvider` does not require a secret type. | **Same** possible. Synthetic provider is constructed directly, with no HTTP client or Secrets. Explicit local-ready startup should replace the misleading credential-presence signal in production. |
39	| Lifecycle | Fixture rejects connect/disconnect/upgrade/sync commands with `InvalidRequest { field: "mode" }`. Gmail disconnect cancels work and clears account/cache. | **Blocker** without fixture admission policy. Preserve errors and prevent synthetic disconnect from erasing local state. |
40	| Mailbox gates | Fixture archives/restores, rejects read/star singles/groups with `ReadOnly`; some other unsupported commands use mode errors. GmailCore's Boolean mutation grant admits all three dimensions (`accept_action`, `accept_operation`). | **Blocker**. Per-session archive-only gate is required at core admission, not only hidden controls. Retain existing error variants initially; consistency is a separate contract change. |
41	| Fake controls | `provider.rs::FakeArchiveProvider::from_env`: paused blocks writes cancellation-aware; reject rejects the next write once; success/default succeeds. | **Different-but-acceptable** implementation: preserve exact environment semantics only in SyntheticProvider writes, leaving reads/bootstrap responsive. Never route the variable to GmailProvider. |
42	| Seed/restart | `store.rs::migrate_and_seed` transaction seeds `conv-01`…`conv-18` once, including archived `conv-06`/`conv-15`; restarts retain facts/history. Gmail discovery fetches Inbox and does not seed archived rows. | **Blocker** without durable synthetic provider state and initial all-seed cache import. A one-time synthetic bootstrap must preserve actual Inbox facts. Existing `GmailCore::load_search_conversation` / `GmailStore::save_search` can preload the two archived seeds explicitly without pretending they are Inbox mail. Ordinary discovery/history intentionally excludes uncached archived bodies (`history_does_not_import_new_archived_thread_bodies_into_the_bounded_cache`). Reopening an in-memory default provider is insufficient. |
43	| Undo/clock | `clock.rs`, both stores and both `open_with_clock` facades use 10 seconds and persisted acceptance/preimages; undo may cancel queued work or enqueue compensation. | **Same** core guarantee. Use injected Clock for deadlines; worker Condvar/Instant scheduling still needs bounded waits/notifications. Preserve strict boundary, immutable targets, partial groups, restart and supersession tests. |
44	| Reminders | `store/reminders.rs::put_reminder` stages archive, worker reconciles removing/pending/returning states and restores prior membership. GmailStore reminders hide locally, do not write provider; no-reply requires connected fresh complete thread read plus account/generation/revision fences (`gmail/sync.rs`, `gmail/store.rs`, UX-11). | **Blocker** to exact parity. Recommended explicit product adjustment: synthetic mode adopts Gmail's local reminder rules, with no Google I/O and fresh reads from the durable synthetic provider. Update fixture disclosures and tests; archive/restore failure-phase tests become obsolete only for that approved adjustment. Do not claim a prototype reminder proves legacy parity. |
45	| Search | `lib.rs::search_mail` / `store.rs::search_mail` evaluate cached fixture data. Gmail `search_mail` can progressively scan provider candidates with bounded incomplete coverage. | **Same** if fixture policy forces cached-only semantics and all 18 are cached; do not silently enable Gmail discovery/search controls. |
46	| Saved split | Both facades/store paths validate and persist one account-scoped split; no provider write or undo supersession. | **Same**, provided account stays `fixture-account`; port restart and undo coexistence assertion. |
47	| Done | Both expose `list_cached_done`, bounded paging, local archive evidence and undo-aware projection. Initially archived rows alone are not necessarily Done evidence. | **Same** guarantee; keep initial seed and pending/restart projection tests. |
48	| Trash/Starred | Fixture rejects cached Trash (`InvalidRequest`, mode) and Starred (`ReadOnly`), has no star UI; Gmail offers observed bounded caches and star setters. | **Blocker** without fixture gates; default SyntheticProvider star/trash facts must not accidentally expose features. |
49	| Destinations | Fixture rejects catalog/page commands with mode errors. Gmail uses account-bound trait methods and separate snapshots. | **Same** with policy rejection; no synthetic destination implementation needed for parity. |
50	| Attachments | Shell fabricates one `fixture-text` descriptor from first message and exact validated text bytes. GmailCore reads persisted descriptors and provider bytes (`list_attachments`, `download_attachment`). | **Different-but-acceptable** ownership: generate the same descriptor/bytes in synthetic data/provider, preserve filename, limits, exact-target revalidation/cancellation and inert Downloads handling. Keep shell transfer security common. |
51	| Reply context | Fixture reader has safe synthetic reply headers; shell checks complete/latest source; Gmail uses cached context then account-fenced metadata enrichment (`load_reply_context`). | **Same** possible by building complete deterministic synthetic reply metadata, including hostile literal bodies, sender identity and references. No network required. |
52	| Local drafts | Shared DraftCore in `<selected-profile>/local-drafts`, revision receipts/tombstones and close flush; account derives from selected backend. | **Same** only if profile path and fixture account/mailbox stay stable. Drafts must survive mailbox reset. |
53	| Pacing/backoff/caps | HTTP provider owns 100ms request spacing (`gmail/provider.rs::pace`); GmailCore owns 60s periodic passes, exponential retry up to 600s, 100 conversation discovery cap, 100 pages/stage, bounded DTO pages. Fixture archive worker has no discovery polling. | **Different-but-acceptable**: SyntheticProvider has no HTTP pacing; 18 fits caps. Seed bootstrap must finish before ready. Fake pause/reject must not stall discovery. Disable needless periodic synthetic discovery or make stable empty history cheap; determinism comes from fixed data, durable facts, injected time and event barriers, not wall-clock sleeps. Explicit requests wake backoff. |
54	
55	No real store bug was established in this investigation. The mismatches above are existing intentional policy differences or prototype limitations; this spike changes none of them.
56	
57	## On-disk transition
58	
59	Today startup selects `<app_data>/fixture-profile/mail.db`; `Store::migrate_and_seed` owns fixture schema versions through 4 and seed version 1. GmailStore opens `gmail.db` with unrelated tables/migrations. Opening that new file beside `mail.db` is not a migration. `docs/development.md` promises seeds never reset provider facts or operation history; `docs/current-status.md` promises durable synthetic state and drafts. A silent reset violates that promise.
60	
61	Choose **reset with disclosure and retained backup**, not an operation-ledger migration, for the eventual implementation. Before changing fixture storage, show a one-time explicit disclosure that synthetic mailbox actions, history, reminders and saved split start fresh; do not automatically approve or execute it as part of this ADR. Keep old `mail.db` and its journal/WAL state safely backed up under the profile lease using a consistent SQLite backup, not a live raw file copy. Record the transition atomically so crashes cannot repeatedly reset the new profile. Never apply this transition to `gmail-profile` or credentials. The implementation must cover cancel, crash/restart, insufficient disk and backup failure before switching.
62	
63	Retain `<fixture-profile>/local-drafts` untouched, along with its account identity and fixture mailbox, so draft references to fixed conversation/message IDs remain meaningful. Do not recursively delete the fixture directory. Test opening old drafts and reply source references after the new seed bootstrap. Update development/status/fixture documentation to state the one-time reset; thereafter retain seed-once/restart persistence. A migration preserving pending preimages/groups/reminder revisions would cost more and needs its own mapping; this proposal deliberately does not promise it.
64	
65	## Wire and frontend contract
66	
67	No DTO shape, generated TypeScript definition, IPC command name or event name needs to change. `dto.rs`, `gmail/types.rs`, `groups.rs`, `reminders.rs`, `src/lib/ipc/client.ts`, `tauri-client.ts` and `generated.ts` can remain the wire source of truth. This spike changes none. A naive switch would change **values and errors** visible on that wire: mode, grant, connection/sync state, coverage count, unsupported command errors and reminder phases. The staged policy must preserve the former values/errors, with the explicitly disclosed local-reminder and initial-loading adjustment above; run generated-contract checks even if no DTO edit is expected.
68	
69	`src/composables/useMailbox.ts` uses mode and mutation access for Gmail upgrade/action controls. `src/lib/browsing-actions.ts` and browser fake controls model Gmail stars/destinations separately. `src/lib/ipc/browser-fake.ts` defaults to fixture, seeds in-memory synthetic conversations, implements simulated-Gmail mode/grants, uses `fixture-text` attachments, fake reply metadata and in-memory operation/reminder ledgers. `fixture-workspaces.ts` also permits overlapping IDs across two isolated synthetic accounts. It remains a browser implementation, not a production provider dependency. Frontend/browser tests establish capability gating, identities, error/receipt rendering, deterministic selection and fake timers; they do not establish SQLite durability, OAuth or native provider behavior. Preserve their fixture/default assumptions and add boundary tests for synthetic native status; do not relabel every browser fixture as Gmail to make tests pass.
70	
71	## Size, risk and fallback
72	
73	Measured source sizes at baseline: fixture `store.rs` 4,030 lines (2,647 before unit tests), `worker.rs` 200, `seed.rs` 327, `provider.rs` 211, fixture `store/reminders.rs` 341; reminder unit/race files 377 combined. Those five principal files total **5,109 lines**, including embedded tests/data; seed data and cancellation infrastructure must move rather than vanish. `lib.rs` is 630 lines (facade/test portions removable, public shared modules remain); the shell Backend implementation occupies about 380 lines plus subscription variants. Including removable facade/shell forwarding, roughly **4,000–4,500 non-test lines removed or replaced**, and roughly **5,000–6,000 gross lines** including relocated tests/data; do not present gross deletion as net savings.
74	
75	Planning estimate, not a prototype diff: add/retain 500–900 lines of production synthetic data/provider persistence, 150–350 lines of session policy/bootstrap and 150–300 lines of transition/disclosure logic, plus 500–1,200 lines of ports/contract tests. Reminder policy work may exceed this. Net production reduction is plausibly 1,000–2,000 lines, contingent on review. Removing 23 duplicated group/undo helpers (~730 lines) is a concrete payoff, not proof the whole rewrite is cheap. Main risks are synthetic facts being overwritten on restart; archived seeds omitted; grants accidentally broadened; reminder semantic drift; draft loss from broad reset; crash-safe backup; shared-core regressions in Gmail; and a long migration with two enabled paths. Each stage must retain working defaults and pass targeted core, contract and native bridge checks; final UI/end-to-end gates belong to the coordinator.
76	
77	If the policy/bootstrap/reminder cost becomes unacceptable, **no-go fallback**: keep both stores and extract only the duplicated ledger algorithms. Define a private `OperationLedgerStorage` seam over an already-owned transaction: load operation/preimage/group rows, enumerate ordered members and newer intent, persist undo decisions/links/receipts, and insert compensation. Shared typed structs carry operation status/dimension/targets, while each adapter owns SQL/table/column names (`operations` vs `gmail_operations`, `failure_kind` vs `last_error`) and row conversion. Pass Clock/now explicitly. Transaction ownership, admission, provider execution, reconciliation and reminder semantics stay in each store; avoid a generic SQL string interpolation framework. Port both existing test matrices before removing helpers. Estimate 250–450 lines of adapters and 100–200 of shared types/glue replacing ~730 duplicated lines (modest net saving), plus a small shell error-policy helper with explicit compatibility tests. It has lower migration risk and no profile reset, but leaves two workers/facades/reminder paths and most shell forwarding. It is a viable smaller ticket if full unification fails its parity gates.
78	
79	## Relationship to PR #44
80	
81	Read `origin/maintenance/p1-rust-test-foundations` at `3814d95` (PR [#44](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/44)), including `testing.rs` and `testing/operations_fake.rs`. Its `test-support` module provides bounded waits/temp profiles/DTO builders and scripted provider outcomes/hooks for cancellation, uncertain dispatch and account races. Use it for ports once merged; rebase in coordinator order. A production SyntheticProvider **must not enable or import test-support** and must not carry its mutable scripts/hooks. Share `GmailReadProvider`, production DTOs and any genuinely pure production data conversion functions in the dependency direction **testing → production**. Fixed fixture data should move from `seed.rs` into a production synthetic module; scripted fakes remain test-only and can wrap the synthetic provider when useful. Do not turn the built-in offline fixture into an arbitrary scripted test engine.
82	
83	
84	## Prototype evidence and limits
85	
86	The separate [throwaway prototype branch](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/tree/maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype) contains only additive test code, based on `58e0bc7`; it is **not for merge**. It constructs `SyntheticProvider` directly and runs real GmailCore/GmailStore SQL, using the repository's actual seed via a test-local path import. There is no Google HTTP client, credentials store, OAuth or Keychain construction. `has_credentials() = true` is a readiness shim that selects startup restore; it does not represent a token. `mutation_access() = true` enables the experiment's archive operations and demonstrates why production needs the separate archive-only policy.
87	
88	Ordinary discovery gives the correct 16-row Inbox. The harness explicitly preloads the two archived seed conversations through `load_search_conversation`; cached search then lists all 18 and the reader checks every fixed ID/subject/message count with the original Inbox facts. The remaining flows use a frozen injected clock: confirmed single archive then compensating Undo; confirmed two-member archive group then group Undo; shutdown and reopen with a **new provider object** reading its saved facts; replay of the same durable SQLite acceptance receipt; and a future local reminder that hides locally then returns after clock advancement. The timer experiment follows Gmail reminder rules, not fixture archive/restore phases.
89	
90	Special cases still required before production: move seed data into a normal production module; make provider facts transactional/crash-durable (the prototype uses non-atomic JSON and defaults missing/malformed JSON to seed facts); model archive per message rather than per conversation; replace readiness/grant shims with explicit fixture policy; replace full-catalog history replay with stable synthetic change tracking; preserve fake pause/reject cancellation semantics; populate synthetic attachments/reply metadata; implement profile transition and port the remaining guarantees below. No test-support feature is enabled or imported. This is evidence that the existing ledger can serve synthetic mail, not evidence of full fixture parity or Gmail/platform correctness.
91	
92	Validated prototype head [`0d6c482daee125c8246daf822db46067fbea6b37`](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/commit/0d6c482daee125c8246daf822db46067fbea6b37): `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target cargo test -p mail-core --test synthetic_provider_spike` — **1 passed, 0 failed**. The one integration test runs every flow above; it is not the full regression suite. Only warning: the path-imported seed module has an unused `SEED_VERSION`. Targeted Rust work was serialized after checking the sibling build slot; no frontend suite or broad Rust build was run for this spike. Production sources, DTOs and lockfile remain unchanged. `git diff --check` passed for the ADR.
93	
94	## Appendix: fixture test disposition
95	
96	This is a source-level map of every `#[test]` in the requested fixture files. **Needs porting** means the synthetic GmailCore path needs an equivalent assertion unless P4's explicit reset/backup decision makes a legacy fixture migration case unreachable. A named Gmail test is listed only where its function name and subject have been checked. Similarity of a broad suite is not treated as coverage.
97	
98	### `crates/mail-core/src/store.rs` (`cfg(test)`)
99	
100	Needs porting: `fixture_reader_has_safe_synthetic_reply_context_without_reseeding` (reader/reply-context safety); `open_fails_closed_on_unusable_profile_directory` (profile initialization failure); `invalid_group_commands_write_nothing` (invalid command atomicity); `member_rejection_is_persisted_and_siblings_accepted_without_undo_slot_loss` (Gmail `gmail_group_member_rejection_is_persisted_and_savepointed` covers persisted rejection and valid sibling replay, but does not assert the fixture's shared Undo-slot condition); `new_reply_after_acceptance_is_untouched_by_group_undo` (new message excluded from Undo targets); `mid_transaction_failure_after_staged_member_rolls_back_whole_group` (atomic rollback after staged child); `worker_claims_and_group_undo_interleave_without_deadlock_or_duplicates` (worker/Undo concurrency); `fresh_v4_seed_marks_first_message_attachment_fact` (fresh profile initial attachment knowledge).
101	
102	Covered by named Gmail tests: `persistence_failure_is_surfaced_not_ignored` → same-named test in `gmail/store.rs`; `group_acceptance_is_idempotent_order_preserving_and_conflict_typed` → `gmail_group_acceptance_is_idempotent_for_archive_and_read`; `transaction_failure_rolls_back_whole_group_and_retry_is_safe` → `gmail_group_storage_failure_rolls_back_and_retry_is_safe`; `group_undo_is_partial_typed_and_one_shot` → `gmail_group_undo_is_partial_typed_and_one_shot`; `group_undo_respects_expiry_supersession_and_no_child_bypass` → `gmail_group_undo_respects_expiry_supersession_and_no_child_bypass`; `group_listing_paginates_and_fences_accounts` → `gmail_group_listing_paginates_and_fences_accounts`; `group_undo_decisions_and_compensation_outcomes_survive_restart` → `gmail_group_undo_record_survives_reopen_with_failed_compensation`. These were checked against test bodies. Their remaining fixture-specific differences are outside the named shared guarantees.
103	
104	Legacy migration cases obsolete under the explicit P4 decision to back up then reset the old `mail.db`, rather than migrate it: `migration_preserves_operations_requests_preimages_and_undo_links`; `authentic_pre_ux05_database_migrates_additively`; `authentic_pre_v4_database_migrates_with_unknown_attachment_facts`; `unsupported_older_schema_version_fails_closed`. The replacement must test backup/reset behavior and fresh-store creation; these tests do not establish those guarantees.
105	
106	`group_undo_decisions_and_compensation_outcomes_survive_restart` is covered by `gmail_group_undo_record_survives_reopen_with_failed_compensation` in `gmail/store.rs`, which reopens the store and checks persisted decisions, failed compensation status and failure kind. The non-group single-operation restart window remains covered by `undoable_until_survives_a_restart_within_the_window_and_expires_after_it` in `crates/mail-core/tests/undo.rs`.
107

# ADR 0002: Fixture mode as a synthetic provider

**Status:** Proposed

## Question and recommendation

Investigate replacing the native fixture store/worker with `GmailCore` and a built-in, credential-free `SyntheticProvider`. This is a decision spike, not authorization to change production behavior. Baseline: `58e0bc7`.

**Recommendation: GO for staged unification; NO-GO for an unmodified provider-only substitution.** GmailCore already accepts `Arc<dyn GmailReadProvider>` and an injected clock. The provider must own durable synthetic provider facts; the core needs a small explicit fixture policy for mode/capabilities/lifecycle and reminders. Keeping a second operation ledger is avoidable, but silently changing the fixture contract is not acceptable. After those gates, delete the fixture `Store`, worker, reminder implementation and `MailCore` facade, and hold one `GmailCore` in shell state with a session policy instead of the `Backend` enum. Move the 18-conversation data out of `seed.rs` into the synthetic module before deleting that file. Retain shared `CancelToken` infrastructure currently located in `provider.rs`; removing the old archive fake must not remove Gmail cancellation support.

## Evidence checkpoints

- Required architecture, status, development and ADR 0001 read. Current docs explicitly promise a separate durable native fixture profile, seed-once behavior, archive-only mailbox actions, local drafts and synthetic attachment transfers.
- `gmail/sync.rs::open_with_clock` has no direct OAuth/Keychain dependency: those belong to the injected production `GmailProvider`. Startup currently interprets `has_credentials()` as a restore signal; a synthetic implementation needs an explicit local-ready policy rather than inventing real credentials.
- `gmail/sync.rs::account_status` hardcodes `MailMode::Gmail`; `mutation_access()` is a Boolean grant covering archive/read/star. Neither preserves fixture wire behavior by itself.
- All requested fixture test files were inventoried by test function name (appendix below). No production files are changed by this spike.

## Implementation stages (each must remain green and shippable)

1. Port fixture-specific guarantees to tests against GmailCore, retain both existing backends, and add a production synthetic data/provider module independent of test support. Keep the default fixture path unchanged.
2. Introduce explicit internal session policy in GmailCore: fixture identity/status, archive-only admission, unsupported errors, cached-only search, local readiness and non-destructive lifecycle. Implement persistent synthetic provider facts and seed-once discovery including the two initially archived conversations. Keep Gmail policy unchanged.
3. Resolve reminder behavior explicitly and cover it with acceptance/race/restart tests; move synthetic attachments/reply metadata behind provider/core seams. Preserve local drafts and fixture profile safety. Add opt-in synthetic-core launch path for validation.
4. Switch fixture default only after all mapped guarantees pass and profile transition disclosure is implemented. Keep the old database as backup. Remove the legacy backend after parity validation; update current docs and browser contract tests. Coordinating thread owns end-to-end validation and merge sequencing.

## Risks and decision gates

A fresh provider seeded into memory on every launch can overwrite archived provider facts at the next sync. Gmail discovery only lists Inbox, so it cannot by itself reproduce the two archived seed threads. GmailCore may expose read/star or destructive disconnect if fixture mode is represented as Gmail. Reminder scheduling currently has different mailbox effects. These are design gates for implementation, not bugs established by this spike.

The prototype will be published separately at [maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/tree/maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype), marked throwaway and not for merge. This PR contains only this ADR.

## Behavior inventory and required policy

References are repository-relative; function names identify the reviewed seam. **Blocker** means an unmodified provider-only substitution cannot preserve the contract. It does not mean the staged implementation is infeasible.

| Surface | Fixture today / GmailCore with synthetic provider | Classification and implementation condition |
|---|---|---|
| Account/status | `src-tauri/src/main.rs::Backend::account_status` returns fixture/Connected/Idle, no mutation grant, 18 cached, complete, no timestamp, limit 0. `gmail/sync.rs::account_status` returns Gmail, observed grant, transient Authenticating/Syncing, timestamps and limit 100. | **Blocker** to drop-in. Internal fixture policy must retain fixture mode/identity/capability presentation; disclose initial loading if asynchronous bootstrap is retained. Do not masquerade as a connected Google account. |
| Credentials | Fixture never opens OAuth or Keychain. GmailCore only calls provider methods; shell constructs GmailProvider/Keychain only in Gmail branch. `gmail/types.rs::GmailReadProvider` does not require a secret type. | **Same** possible. Synthetic provider is constructed directly, with no HTTP client or Secrets. Explicit local-ready startup should replace the misleading credential-presence signal in production. |
| Lifecycle | Fixture rejects connect/disconnect/upgrade/sync commands with `InvalidRequest { field: "mode" }`. Gmail disconnect cancels work and clears account/cache. | **Blocker** without fixture admission policy. Preserve errors and prevent synthetic disconnect from erasing local state. |
| Mailbox gates | Fixture archives/restores, rejects read/star singles/groups with `ReadOnly`; some other unsupported commands use mode errors. GmailCore's Boolean mutation grant admits all three dimensions (`accept_action`, `accept_operation`). | **Blocker**. Per-session archive-only gate is required at core admission, not only hidden controls. Retain existing error variants initially; consistency is a separate contract change. |
| Fake controls | `provider.rs::FakeArchiveProvider::from_env`: paused blocks writes cancellation-aware; reject rejects the next write once; success/default succeeds. | **Different-but-acceptable** implementation: preserve exact environment semantics only in SyntheticProvider writes, leaving reads/bootstrap responsive. Never route the variable to GmailProvider. |
| Seed/restart | `store.rs::migrate_and_seed` transaction seeds `conv-01`…`conv-18` once, including archived `conv-06`/`conv-15`; restarts retain facts/history. Gmail discovery fetches Inbox and does not seed archived rows. | **Blocker** without durable synthetic provider state and initial all-seed cache import. A one-time synthetic bootstrap must preserve actual Inbox facts. Existing `GmailCore::load_search_conversation` / `GmailStore::save_search` can preload the two archived seeds explicitly without pretending they are Inbox mail. Ordinary discovery/history intentionally excludes uncached archived bodies (`history_does_not_import_new_archived_thread_bodies_into_the_bounded_cache`). Reopening an in-memory default provider is insufficient. |
| Undo/clock | `clock.rs`, both stores and both `open_with_clock` facades use 10 seconds and persisted acceptance/preimages; undo may cancel queued work or enqueue compensation. | **Same** core guarantee. Use injected Clock for deadlines; worker Condvar/Instant scheduling still needs bounded waits/notifications. Preserve strict boundary, immutable targets, partial groups, restart and supersession tests. |
| Reminders | `store/reminders.rs::put_reminder` stages archive, worker reconciles removing/pending/returning states and restores prior membership. GmailStore reminders hide locally, do not write provider; no-reply requires connected fresh complete thread read plus account/generation/revision fences (`gmail/sync.rs`, `gmail/store.rs`, UX-11). | **Blocker** to exact parity. Recommended explicit product adjustment: synthetic mode adopts Gmail's local reminder rules, with no Google I/O and fresh reads from the durable synthetic provider. Update fixture disclosures and tests; archive/restore failure-phase tests become obsolete only for that approved adjustment. Do not claim a prototype reminder proves legacy parity. |
| Search | `lib.rs::search_mail` / `store.rs::search_mail` evaluate cached fixture data. Gmail `search_mail` can progressively scan provider candidates with bounded incomplete coverage. | **Same** if fixture policy forces cached-only semantics and all 18 are cached; do not silently enable Gmail discovery/search controls. |
| Saved split | Both facades/store paths validate and persist one account-scoped split; no provider write or undo supersession. | **Same**, provided account stays `fixture-account`; port restart and undo coexistence assertion. |
| Done | Both expose `list_cached_done`, bounded paging, local archive evidence and undo-aware projection. Initially archived rows alone are not necessarily Done evidence. | **Same** guarantee; keep initial seed and pending/restart projection tests. |
| Trash/Starred | Fixture rejects cached Trash (`InvalidRequest`, mode) and Starred (`ReadOnly`), has no star UI; Gmail offers observed bounded caches and star setters. | **Blocker** without fixture gates; default SyntheticProvider star/trash facts must not accidentally expose features. |
| Destinations | Fixture rejects catalog/page commands with mode errors. Gmail uses account-bound trait methods and separate snapshots. | **Same** with policy rejection; no synthetic destination implementation needed for parity. |
| Attachments | Shell fabricates one `fixture-text` descriptor from first message and exact validated text bytes. GmailCore reads persisted descriptors and provider bytes (`list_attachments`, `download_attachment`). | **Different-but-acceptable** ownership: generate the same descriptor/bytes in synthetic data/provider, preserve filename, limits, exact-target revalidation/cancellation and inert Downloads handling. Keep shell transfer security common. |
| Reply context | Fixture reader has safe synthetic reply headers; shell checks complete/latest source; Gmail uses cached context then account-fenced metadata enrichment (`load_reply_context`). | **Same** possible by building complete deterministic synthetic reply metadata, including hostile literal bodies, sender identity and references. No network required. |
| Local drafts | Shared DraftCore in `<selected-profile>/local-drafts`, revision receipts/tombstones and close flush; account derives from selected backend. | **Same** only if profile path and fixture account/mailbox stay stable. Drafts must survive mailbox reset. |
| Pacing/backoff/caps | HTTP provider owns 100ms request spacing (`gmail/provider.rs::pace`); GmailCore owns 60s periodic passes, exponential retry up to 600s, 100 conversation discovery cap, 100 pages/stage, bounded DTO pages. Fixture archive worker has no discovery polling. | **Different-but-acceptable**: SyntheticProvider has no HTTP pacing; 18 fits caps. Seed bootstrap must finish before ready. Fake pause/reject must not stall discovery. Disable needless periodic synthetic discovery or make stable empty history cheap; determinism comes from fixed data, durable facts, injected time and event barriers, not wall-clock sleeps. Explicit requests wake backoff. |

No real store bug was established in this investigation. The mismatches above are existing intentional policy differences or prototype limitations; this spike changes none of them.

## On-disk transition

Today startup selects `<app_data>/fixture-profile/mail.db`; `Store::migrate_and_seed` owns fixture schema versions through 4 and seed version 1. GmailStore opens `gmail.db` with unrelated tables/migrations. Opening that new file beside `mail.db` is not a migration. `docs/development.md` promises seeds never reset provider facts or operation history; `docs/current-status.md` promises durable synthetic state and drafts. A silent reset violates that promise.

Choose **reset with disclosure and retained backup**, not an operation-ledger migration, for the eventual implementation. Before changing fixture storage, show a one-time explicit disclosure that synthetic mailbox actions, history, reminders and saved split start fresh; do not automatically approve or execute it as part of this ADR. Keep old `mail.db` and its journal/WAL state safely backed up under the profile lease using a consistent SQLite backup, not a live raw file copy. Record the transition atomically so crashes cannot repeatedly reset the new profile. Never apply this transition to `gmail-profile` or credentials. The implementation must cover cancel, crash/restart, insufficient disk and backup failure before switching.

Retain `<fixture-profile>/local-drafts` untouched, along with its account identity and fixture mailbox, so draft references to fixed conversation/message IDs remain meaningful. Do not recursively delete the fixture directory. Test opening old drafts and reply source references after the new seed bootstrap. Update development/status/fixture documentation to state the one-time reset; thereafter retain seed-once/restart persistence. A migration preserving pending preimages/groups/reminder revisions would cost more and needs its own mapping; this proposal deliberately does not promise it.

## Wire and frontend contract

No DTO shape, generated TypeScript definition, IPC command name or event name needs to change. `dto.rs`, `gmail/types.rs`, `groups.rs`, `reminders.rs`, `src/lib/ipc/client.ts`, `tauri-client.ts` and `generated.ts` can remain the wire source of truth. This spike changes none. A naive switch would change **values and errors** visible on that wire: mode, grant, connection/sync state, coverage count, unsupported command errors and reminder phases. The staged policy must preserve the former values/errors, with the explicitly disclosed local-reminder and initial-loading adjustment above; run generated-contract checks even if no DTO edit is expected.

`src/composables/useMailbox.ts` uses mode and mutation access for Gmail upgrade/action controls. `src/lib/browsing-actions.ts` and browser fake controls model Gmail stars/destinations separately. `src/lib/ipc/browser-fake.ts` defaults to fixture, seeds in-memory synthetic conversations, implements simulated-Gmail mode/grants, uses `fixture-text` attachments, fake reply metadata and in-memory operation/reminder ledgers. `fixture-workspaces.ts` also permits overlapping IDs across two isolated synthetic accounts. It remains a browser implementation, not a production provider dependency. Frontend/browser tests establish capability gating, identities, error/receipt rendering, deterministic selection and fake timers; they do not establish SQLite durability, OAuth or native provider behavior. Preserve their fixture/default assumptions and add boundary tests for synthetic native status; do not relabel every browser fixture as Gmail to make tests pass.

## Size, risk and fallback

Measured source sizes at baseline: fixture `store.rs` 4,030 lines (2,647 before unit tests), `worker.rs` 200, `seed.rs` 327, `provider.rs` 211, fixture `store/reminders.rs` 341; reminder unit/race files 377 combined. Those five principal files total **5,109 lines**, including embedded tests/data; seed data and cancellation infrastructure must move rather than vanish. `lib.rs` is 630 lines (facade/test portions removable, public shared modules remain); the shell Backend implementation occupies about 380 lines plus subscription variants. Including removable facade/shell forwarding, roughly **4,000–4,500 non-test lines removed or replaced**, and roughly **5,000–6,000 gross lines** including relocated tests/data; do not present gross deletion as net savings.

Planning estimate, not a prototype diff: add/retain 500–900 lines of production synthetic data/provider persistence, 150–350 lines of session policy/bootstrap and 150–300 lines of transition/disclosure logic, plus 500–1,200 lines of ports/contract tests. Reminder policy work may exceed this. Net production reduction is plausibly 1,000–2,000 lines, contingent on review. Removing 23 duplicated group/undo helpers (~730 lines) is a concrete payoff, not proof the whole rewrite is cheap. Main risks are synthetic facts being overwritten on restart; archived seeds omitted; grants accidentally broadened; reminder semantic drift; draft loss from broad reset; crash-safe backup; shared-core regressions in Gmail; and a long migration with two enabled paths. Each stage must retain working defaults and pass targeted core, contract and native bridge checks; final UI/end-to-end gates belong to the coordinator.

If the policy/bootstrap/reminder cost becomes unacceptable, **no-go fallback**: keep both stores and extract only the duplicated ledger algorithms. Define a private `OperationLedgerStorage` seam over an already-owned transaction: load operation/preimage/group rows, enumerate ordered members and newer intent, persist undo decisions/links/receipts, and insert compensation. Shared typed structs carry operation status/dimension/targets, while each adapter owns SQL/table/column names (`operations` vs `gmail_operations`, `failure_kind` vs `last_error`) and row conversion. Pass Clock/now explicitly. Transaction ownership, admission, provider execution, reconciliation and reminder semantics stay in each store; avoid a generic SQL string interpolation framework. Port both existing test matrices before removing helpers. Estimate 250–450 lines of adapters and 100–200 of shared types/glue replacing ~730 duplicated lines (modest net saving), plus a small shell error-policy helper with explicit compatibility tests. It has lower migration risk and no profile reset, but leaves two workers/facades/reminder paths and most shell forwarding. It is a viable smaller ticket if full unification fails its parity gates.

## Relationship to PR #44

Read `origin/maintenance/p1-rust-test-foundations` at `3814d95` (PR [#44](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/44)), including `testing.rs` and `testing/operations_fake.rs`. Its `test-support` module provides bounded waits/temp profiles/DTO builders and scripted provider outcomes/hooks for cancellation, uncertain dispatch and account races. Use it for ports once merged; rebase in coordinator order. A production SyntheticProvider **must not enable or import test-support** and must not carry its mutable scripts/hooks. Share `GmailReadProvider`, production DTOs and any genuinely pure production data conversion functions in the dependency direction **testing → production**. Fixed fixture data should move from `seed.rs` into a production synthetic module; scripted fakes remain test-only and can wrap the synthetic provider when useful. Do not turn the built-in offline fixture into an arbitrary scripted test engine.


## Prototype evidence and limits

The separate [throwaway prototype branch](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/tree/maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype) contains only additive test code, based on `58e0bc7`; it is **not for merge**. It constructs `SyntheticProvider` directly and runs real GmailCore/GmailStore SQL, using the repository's actual seed via a test-local path import. There is no Google HTTP client, credentials store, OAuth or Keychain construction. `has_credentials() = true` is a readiness shim that selects startup restore; it does not represent a token. `mutation_access() = true` enables the experiment's archive operations and demonstrates why production needs the separate archive-only policy.

Ordinary discovery gives the correct 16-row Inbox. The harness explicitly preloads the two archived seed conversations through `load_search_conversation`; cached search then lists all 18 and the reader checks every fixed ID/subject/message count with the original Inbox facts. The remaining flows use a frozen injected clock: confirmed single archive then compensating Undo; confirmed two-member archive group then group Undo; shutdown and reopen with a **new provider object** reading its saved facts; replay of the same durable SQLite acceptance receipt; and a future local reminder that hides locally then returns after clock advancement. The timer experiment follows Gmail reminder rules, not fixture archive/restore phases.

Special cases still required before production: move seed data into a normal production module; make provider facts transactional/crash-durable (the prototype uses non-atomic JSON and defaults missing/malformed JSON to seed facts); model archive per message rather than per conversation; replace readiness/grant shims with explicit fixture policy; replace full-catalog history replay with stable synthetic change tracking; preserve fake pause/reject cancellation semantics; populate synthetic attachments/reply metadata; implement profile transition and port the remaining guarantees below. No test-support feature is enabled or imported. This is evidence that the existing ledger can serve synthetic mail, not evidence of full fixture parity or Gmail/platform correctness.

Validated prototype head [`0d6c482daee125c8246daf822db46067fbea6b37`](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/commit/0d6c482daee125c8246daf822db46067fbea6b37): `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target cargo test -p mail-core --test synthetic_provider_spike` — **1 passed, 0 failed**. The one integration test runs every flow above; it is not the full regression suite. Only warning: the path-imported seed module has an unused `SEED_VERSION`. Targeted Rust work was serialized after checking the sibling build slot; no frontend suite or broad Rust build was run for this spike. Production sources, DTOs and lockfile remain unchanged. `git diff --check` passed for the ADR.

## Appendix: fixture test disposition

This is a source-level map of every `#[test]` in the requested fixture files. **Needs porting** means the synthetic GmailCore path needs an equivalent assertion unless P4's explicit reset/backup decision makes a legacy fixture migration case unreachable. A named Gmail test is listed only where its function name and subject have been checked. Similarity of a broad suite is not treated as coverage.

### `crates/mail-core/src/store.rs` (`cfg(test)`)

[package]
name = "mail-core"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.89"
description = "Headless fixture and Gmail mail core: SQLite stores, provider sync and operations, serde/ts-rs DTOs"
license = "UNLICENSED"

[features]
test-support = ["dep:tempfile"]

[dependencies]
rusqlite = { version = "0.37", features = ["bundled"] }
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
ts-rs = { version = "11", features = ["serde-compat", "no-serde-warnings"] }
uuid = { version = "1", features = ["v4"] }
thiserror = "2"
chrono = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["clock"] }
reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false, features = ["blocking", "json", "rustls-tls"] }
base64 = "0.22"
rand = "0.8"
sha2 = "0.10"
url = "2"
log = "0.4"
mailparse = "0.16"
charset = "0.1"
webbrowser = "1"
tempfile = { version = "3", optional = true }

[dev-dependencies]
tempfile = "3"
mail_core = { package = "mail-core", path = ".", features = ["test-support"] }

[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]
keyring = { version = "3", default-features = false, features = ["apple-native"] }

[[bin]]
name = "generate-types"
path = "src/bin/generate-types.rs"
archive-idempotent-replay.json
archive-single-confirmed.json
archive-undo-restores-only-originally-inbox-messages.json
fixture-rejects-unsupported-commands.json
group-and-single-actions-supersede-each-other.json
group-archive-mixed-membership.json
group-idempotent-replay.json
group-member-failure-does-not-stop-siblings.json
group-size-cap.json
group-undo-cancels-queued-members.json
group-undo-partial-results.json
group-undo-rejected-after-the-window.json
group-undo-without-an-eligible-member.json
invalid-commands.json
mailboxes.json
read-and-star-groups.json
read-setter-and-undo.json
retry-of-a-failed-operation.json
star-setter-and-undo.json
star-with-unknown-prior-is-not-undoable.json
unarchive-restores-inbox.json
undo-cancels-a-queued-operation.json
undo-compensates-a-claimed-operation.json
undo-compensates-a-confirmed-operation.json
undo-rejected-after-the-window.json
undo-rejected-for-a-failed-operation.json
undo-rejected-when-superseded.json
[tools]
node = "24.4.1"
pnpm = "10.18.0"
rust = { version = "1.89.0", profile = "minimal", components = "rustfmt,clippy" }

[tasks."setup:linux"]
description = "Install Debian/Ubuntu VM prerequisites for native builds and screenshots (uses apt-get)"
run = '''
set -eu
if [ "$(uname -s)" != Linux ]; then
  echo "setup:linux requires Linux with apt-get (Debian/Ubuntu); macOS setup is unchanged." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "setup:linux requires apt-get. Install the prerequisites for your distribution manually; see docs/development.md." >&2
  exit 1
fi
set -- apt-get
if [ "$(id -u)" != 0 ]; then
  if ! command -v sudo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "setup:linux requires root or sudo to install OS packages." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  set -- sudo apt-get
fi
"$@" update
"$@" install -y build-essential pkg-config libglib2.0-dev libgtk-3-dev libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev librsvg2-dev dbus-daemon xvfb xauth xdotool openbox x11-utils scrot
'''

[tasks."install:ui"]
description = "Install locked frontend dependencies"
run = "pnpm install --frozen-lockfile"

[tasks."test:core"]
description = "Test the headless mail core"
run = "cargo test --locked -p mail-core"

[tasks."gen:ts"]
description = "Generate src/lib/ipc/generated.ts from the Rust DTOs"
run = "cargo run --locked -q -p mail-core --bin generate-types -- src/lib/ipc/generated.ts"

[tasks."check:contract"]
description = "Fail when src/lib/ipc/generated.ts drifts from the Rust DTOs"
run = """
dir=$(mktemp -d)
tmp="$dir/generated.ts"
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"; rmdir "$dir"' EXIT
cargo run --locked -q -p mail-core --bin generate-types -- "$tmp"
diff -u src/lib/ipc/generated.ts "$tmp"
"""

[tasks."lint:core"]
description = "Workspace formatting and mail-core clippy checks with warnings denied"
run = "cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --locked -p mail-core --all-targets -- -D warnings"

[tasks."lint:native"]
description = "Clippy checks for the native shell and all targets with warnings denied (needs GTK/WebKit dev prerequisites)"
run = "cargo clippy --locked -p email-os --all-targets -- -D warnings"

[tasks."test:ui"]
description = "Run frontend component and contract tests"
run = "pnpm test"

[tasks.typecheck]
description = "Typecheck the Vue frontend"
run = "pnpm typecheck"

[tasks."build:web"]
description = "Build the frontend assets for browser preview and native shell"
run = "pnpm build"

[tasks."dev:web"]
description = "Run the synthetic in-memory browser preview"
run = "pnpm dev"

[tasks."dev:native"]
description = "Run the native shell (synthetic fixture default; Gmail starts read-only until mailbox actions are enabled)"
run = "pnpm tauri dev"

[tasks."build:native"]

[package]
name = "mail-core"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.89"
description = "Headless fixture and Gmail mail core: SQLite stores, provider sync and operations, serde/ts-rs DTOs"
license = "UNLICENSED"

[features]
test-support = ["dep:tempfile"]

[dependencies]
rusqlite = { version = "0.37", features = ["bundled"] }
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
ts-rs = { version = "11", features = ["serde-compat", "no-serde-warnings"] }
uuid = { version = "1", features = ["v4"] }
thiserror = "2"
chrono = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["clock"] }
reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false, features = ["blocking", "json", "rustls-tls"] }
base64 = "0.22"
rand = "0.8"
sha2 = "0.10"
url = "2"
log = "0.4"
mailparse = "0.16"
charset = "0.1"
webbrowser = "1"
tempfile = { version = "3", optional = true }

[dev-dependencies]
tempfile = "3"
mail_core = { package = "mail-core", path = ".", features = ["test-support"] }

[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]
keyring = { version = "3", default-features = false, features = ["apple-native"] }

[[bin]]
name = "generate-types"
path = "src/bin/generate-types.rs"
archive-idempotent-replay.json
archive-single-confirmed.json
archive-undo-restores-only-originally-inbox-messages.json
fixture-rejects-unsupported-commands.json
group-and-single-actions-supersede-each-other.json
group-archive-mixed-membership.json
group-idempotent-replay.json
group-member-failure-does-not-stop-siblings.json
group-size-cap.json
group-undo-cancels-queued-members.json
group-undo-partial-results.json
group-undo-rejected-after-the-window.json
group-undo-without-an-eligible-member.json
invalid-commands.json
mailboxes.json
read-and-star-groups.json
read-setter-and-undo.json
retry-of-a-failed-operation.json
star-setter-and-undo.json
star-with-unknown-prior-is-not-undoable.json
unarchive-restores-inbox.json
undo-cancels-a-queued-operation.json
undo-compensates-a-claimed-operation.json
undo-compensates-a-confirmed-operation.json
undo-rejected-after-the-window.json
undo-rejected-for-a-failed-operation.json
undo-rejected-when-superseded.json
[tools]
node = "24.4.1"
pnpm = "10.18.0"
rust = { version = "1.89.0", profile = "minimal", components = "rustfmt,clippy" }

[tasks."setup:linux"]
description = "Install Debian/Ubuntu VM prerequisites for native builds and screenshots (uses apt-get)"
run = '''
set -eu
if [ "$(uname -s)" != Linux ]; then
  echo "setup:linux requires Linux with apt-get (Debian/Ubuntu); macOS setup is unchanged." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "setup:linux requires apt-get. Install the prerequisites for your distribution manually; see docs/development.md." >&2
  exit 1
fi
set -- apt-get
if [ "$(id -u)" != 0 ]; then
  if ! command -v sudo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "setup:linux requires root or sudo to install OS packages." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  set -- sudo apt-get
fi
"$@" update
"$@" install -y build-essential pkg-config libglib2.0-dev libgtk-3-dev libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev librsvg2-dev dbus-daemon xvfb xauth xdotool openbox x11-utils scrot
'''

[tasks."install:ui"]
description = "Install locked frontend dependencies"
run = "pnpm install --frozen-lockfile"

[tasks."test:core"]
description = "Test the headless mail core"
run = "cargo test --locked -p mail-core"

[tasks."gen:ts"]
description = "Generate src/lib/ipc/generated.ts from the Rust DTOs"
run = "cargo run --locked -q -p mail-core --bin generate-types -- src/lib/ipc/generated.ts"

[tasks."check:contract"]
description = "Fail when src/lib/ipc/generated.ts drifts from the Rust DTOs"
run = """
dir=$(mktemp -d)
tmp="$dir/generated.ts"

cargo run --locked -q -p mail-core --bin generate-types -- "$tmp"
diff -u src/lib/ipc/generated.ts "$tmp"
"""

[tasks."lint:core"]
description = "Workspace formatting and mail-core clippy checks with warnings denied"
run = "cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --locked -p mail-core --all-targets -- -D warnings"

[tasks."lint:native"]
description = "Clippy checks for the native shell and all targets with warnings denied (needs GTK/WebKit dev prerequisites)"
run = "cargo clippy --locked -p email-os --all-targets -- -D warnings"

[tasks."test:ui"]
description = "Run frontend component and contract tests"
run = "pnpm test"

[tasks.typecheck]
description = "Typecheck the Vue frontend"
run = "pnpm typecheck"

[tasks."build:web"]
description = "Build the frontend assets for browser preview and native shell"
run = "pnpm build"

[tasks."dev:web"]
description = "Run the synthetic in-memory browser preview"
run = "pnpm dev"

[tasks."dev:native"]
description = "Run the native shell (synthetic fixture default; Gmail starts read-only until mailbox actions are enabled)"
run = "pnpm tauri dev"

[tasks."build:native"]

I'm checking how archived threads that aren't in the cache yet get picked up, since they won't be upserted from the inbox. So I'll need to load them with `load_search_conversation` and save them through `save_search`, which should also add them to the conversation count. I'm also starting to look at what happens when an inbox conversation is archived through the ledger and then gets picked up by discovery on the next pass.

I'm working through when discovery gets rerun after an archived conversation is picked up again. Discovery returns Done right away, so history runs from the cursor, and I'll need synthetic change tracking so that an unchanged history returns an empty page cheaply. I'm also weighing whether the periodic sync should skip ticks for the synthetic provider.

I'm weighing how big stage 1 should be: the ADR decisions, a production synthetic data module with a SyntheticGmailProvider, ported tests against GmailCore, and the KD-3 fix in the fake. The open question is how GmailCore runs without a session policy, since the provider will need stand-ins for readiness and mutation access until stage 2 replaces them.

I'm settling on a stage 1 shape where the synthetic provider answers `has_credentials` and `mutation_access` as local-ready facts, just so the trait still works. Stage 2's session policy will take over those checks, and these answers will go unused by the synthetic path.

I'm sketching what the session policy should look like in stage 2, with a gmail and a synthetic variant that each decide readiness, mutation admission and the mode.

I'm sketching the stage 2 session policy as a trait with Gmail and synthetic implementations, so Gmail stays untouched, and the synthetic one will get its own open constructor and a fixture account identity.

I'm weighing whether to run the first sync synchronously during open, so the list isn't empty while an asynchronous bootstrap is still running.

I'm weighing whether to run the first bootstrap synchronously inside open, so the session starts already connected and the list is never empty. That would call the pass directly with the restore action before the worker spawns, and an error there would fail open instead of leaving a loading state.

I'm now weighing a restart: the bootstrap should be safe to run again on reopen, since the account begin is idempotent and history picks up from the cursor. The open question is how the archived-conversation preload stays one-time without a durable marker.

I'm planning to run the bootstrap in a private method that preloads seed conversations missing from the cache, checking each with get_conversation and saving it when it's absent. That keeps it idempotent without a marker. I'm weighing whether to call the public load_search_conversation, which needs a Connected status and reply enrichment, but since I'm bootstrapping synchronously before the worker starts, I already have the control handle I need.

I'm checking whether `save_search` marks the threads as search cache, and whether `list_cached_done` would pick up those conversations without any Done evidence. I'm also wondering if search cache entries get trimmed once the count grows.

content.thinking:
I'm checking that finished-state evidence only comes from operations, so rows that start out archived don't count as done. The search cache holds just two entries against its cap of 100, and it survives discovery. If the user later restores conv-06 to the inbox, the upsert with non-empty inbox ids removes it from the cache, which is fine. I'm also weighing whether the provider's list_inbox should return archived threads too, but I'm leaning against that.

I'm sketching a synthetic Gmail provider that keeps only its mutable facts (inbox, unread, starred per message) in a small SQLite file, with a change log keyed by history id. Message content stays in static constants, and the seed runs once inside a transaction.

I'm working out what the fixture should report for read state, since it currently has none and ConversationSummary's is_read is optional. Seeding every message as unread would clutter the inbox, so I'm leaning toward treating messages I sent as already read and others as unread, then checking how the gmail store derives is_read.

I'm deciding the initial read state for the seeded messages: marking messages from me as read and the rest as unread for inbox conversations, which makes the read controls demonstrable but changes what the inbox shows. I'm also checking what the star facts should start as.

I'm settling on the synthetic provider's trash and spam sets as empty lists, and the full message id set as the complete inventory. For the history id, I'm weighing whether to use the maximum change id as a string, with seed time leaving it at the starting value.

I'm working out how history and writes will behave: each change bumps a counter and records the affected conversation, so a history query returns the conversations changed since a given id, and an unparseable or too-new start is treated as expired. I'm also settling how archive and unarchive writes apply to inbox facts inside a single transaction.

I'm checking how the provider's env switch behaves, since the pause semantics will decide how cancelled work ends up as outcome_unknown and gets reconciled at restart.

python3 - <<'EOF'
p='docs/adr/0002-fixture-as-synthetic-provider.md'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("**Status:** Proposed\n","**Status:** Accepted (stages 1–3)\n",1)
dec='''## Decisions

Taken on 2026-11-14 on the coordinating thread's recommendation, after the project owner asked for the remaining maintenance tickets to run. They authorise **stages 1 to 3** only. The owner can still redirect before stage 4 (switching the default and deleting the legacy backend); nothing below is a user-facing change until then.

1. **Staged unification**, as recommended above. The legacy `MailCore` backend stays the default and is not touched until stage 4.
2. **The unified fixture gains read and star.** Synthetic fixture mode admits archive, read and star (single and group), and the cached Starred list works. This departs from the "archive-only" wording in the stages and inventory below, which was about preserving today's errors. Cached Trash and provider destinations stay rejected with today's error variants. Connect, disconnect, permission upgrade and manual sync stay rejected with `InvalidRequest { field: "mode" }`, and nothing in synthetic mode may erase local state the way a Gmail disconnect does.
3. **Synthetic reminders follow the Gmail core's local rules** (hide locally, no provider write). The legacy fixture's archive/restore reminder phases are retired when stage 4 lands, not before.
4. **The on-disk transition (stage 4) is a one-time reset with disclosure and a retained backup**, local drafts untouched. It is planned, not implemented, in stages 1–3.

Unchanged by these decisions: wire mode stays `fixture`, the account stays `fixture-account`, no OAuth, no Keychain, no HTTP client, cached-only search, all 18 conversations present (including the two initially archived `conv-06` and `conv-15`), and the fake pause/reject environment controls apply only to synthetic writes and never reach the live provider.

'''
s=s.replace("## Question and recommendation\n",dec+"## Question and recommendation\n",1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

Records the ADR 0002 decisions and accepts stages 1-3.
